title: Assurance bridge matrix and log-export playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a practitioner-oriented bridge matrix and runbook to prepare artifacts and responses for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 auditors focused on RBAC v2, audit log schema, automated evidence exports, and SIEM integration. It synthesizes control mappings, identified gaps, prioritized fixes, sample SIEM queries, and auditor-friendly Q&A scripts so on-call engineers and the compliance team can rapidly assemble a coherent evidence package.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated control-plane components, RBAC v2 control plane, API audit exports, and SIEM ingestion pipeline.
- Assumes RBAC change tracking is implemented in the control plane but not all exports were previously wired to the SIEM for long-tail retention.
- Target auditors: external SOC 2 / ISO assessors performing control walkthroughs and evidence sampling.

High-level approach:
1) Map each relevant control to 1–3 canonical artifacts (logs, config snapshots, PRs, runbooks).
2) Identify concrete evidence gaps and assign remediation owners with deadlines.
3) Create reproducible SIEM queries and export snapshots for auditor sampling.
4) Draft short Q&A scripts and link artifacts by stable id/URL.

Control mapping summary (examples):
- SOC 2 CC6.1 / ISO A.9.2 (Access provisioning):
  - Primary evidence: RBAC change log export (audit_log.type="rbac_change"), provisioning PRs, approval ticket.
  - Secondary evidence: periodic access review spreadsheet, CSV export from access-review tool.
- SOC 2 CC7.1 / ISO A.12.4 (Logging & monitoring):
  - Primary evidence: SIEM index with control-plane audit logs (retention policy), alert runbook references, sample raw log bundle.
- SOC 2 CC3.2 (Change management):
  - Primary evidence: GitHub PRs + CI/CD deploy event logs (deploy.user, deploy.tag, deploy.timestamp).

Key gaps identified (snapshot):
- G1 (High): No stable, long-term export configured for RBAC change logs older than 90 days in SIEM. Current retention only 30d in ingests. (Owner: Priya Nair)
- G2 (Medium): Audit log schema missing explicit "actor_role" normalized field (makes auditor correlation manual). (Owner: Ethan Kim)
- G3 (Low): Evidence naming is inconsistent — artifacts in Drive lack canonical IDs for auditors to reference. (Owner: Jordan Liu)

Prioritized remediation plan (practical steps):
- G1 remediation (2 weeks):
  - Task A: Enable daily export job from control plane -> S3-archive-bucket -> SIEM-collector with 90d lifecycle. (JIRA: SC-487)
  - Task B: Validate export integrity using automated checksum and sample rehydrate test.
- G2 remediation (1 sprint):
  - Task A: Extend audit logging middleware to emit actor_role and actor_id in normalized fields. Deploy behind feature-flag.
  - Task B: Backfill last 30 days via transformation job (map complex principal structures to role names).
- G3 remediation (ongoing):
  - Task: Adopt canonical artifact naming convention: {control}-{artifact-type}-{YYYYMMDD}-{id}.

Auditor Q&A scripts (short, ready-to-read):
Q: How are RBAC changes recorded and who approves them?
A: All RBAC mutations go through the control plane API and are recorded as immutable audit_log entries (type=rbac_change). Approval is captured in the provisioning ticket (linked JIRA) and reflected in the pull request title and the audit entry metadata (approval.ticket_id). See artifacts: CONFLUENCE-SEC-2312, JIRA-SC-487, audit-export-2025-02-20.zip.

Q: How long are control-plane logs retained and how can you provide historical entries?
A: Active SIEM ingestion retains 90 days hot index; we also archive daily bundles to S3 with 1 year retention for audit purposes. For this audit we will provide S3 rehydrated bundles for requested sampling windows.

Q: How do you prove the integrity of exported logs?
A: Each daily export is produced with a SHA256 manifest. The export pipeline stores manifests in an immutable prefix in the archive bucket and supports deterministic rehydration. See runbook step 4 (content below) and sample manifest: export-2025-02-20.manifest.sha256.

Evidence artefacts to prepare (minimum set):
- RBAC change log exported JSONL (sample 100 lines) -> artifact id: audit-export-2025-02-20.jsonl
- SIEM query result (90-day window) -> artifact id: siem-result-2025-02.json.csv
- Access review CSV for Q4 -> artifact id: access-review-q4-2024.csv
- Relevant PRs and deploy logs -> links to GitHub PRs and CI logs
- Runbooks: rbac-change-walkthrough.md, log-export-runbook.md

Evidence acceptance criteria (auditor-friendly checklist):
- Timestamp present and verified (ISO8601).
- Immutable event id present.
- Actor identity and actor_role present (or mapping provided).
- Export manifest SHA256 included and matches content.
- If requested sampling window outside hot retention, archived bundle available and rehydration validated.

SIEM export and sampling runbook (step-by-step):
1) Identify sample window and scope (e.g., 2024-11-01 to 2024-11-30).
2) Run SIEM query (examples below) and export raw JSON/CSV.
3) Snapshot S3 archive for same window and verify checksums.
4) Produce a redacted sample set (PII removed) and provide mapping of original->redacted in a separate manifest for auditors.
5) Upload packaged artifacts to secured auditor share and record links in the artifact index doc.

Sample SIEM queries (Elastic / Splunk style) - adapt to your SIEM: 
- Elastic DSL (pseudo):
  GET /_search?q=event.type:rbac_change AND timestamp:[2024-11-01 TO 2024-11-30]&size=10000
- Splunk SPL (pseudo):
  index=controlplane source=audit_logs "rbac_change" | where _time>=strptime("2024-11-01","%Y-%m-%d") AND _time<strptime("2024-12-01","%Y-%m-%d") | table _time, event_id, actor_id, actor_role, change.diff

Sample audit log line (JSON):
{"event_id":"evt-01F3","timestamp":"2024-11-12T15:22:11Z","type":"rbac_change","actor_id":"user-983","actor_role":"admin","target_principal":"service-account-scheduler","change":{"before":"read","after":"write"},"approval":{"ticket_id":"SC-201","approver":"lead-platform"}}

Log schema mapping (what fields map to which control evidence):
- event_id -> immutability proof (SOC 2 CC7.1)
- timestamp -> timeline reconstruction (ISO A.12.4)
- type -> control classification (supports multiple controls e.g., access/change)
- actor_id + actor_role -> identity & segregation evidence (SOC 2 CC6.1)
- change -> demonstrates action taken (change management)
- approval.ticket_id -> evidence of prior authorization (change control)

Automation checklist for export pipeline (run once per audit request):
- [ ] Ensure feature-flag for normalized fields enabled in staging and prod.
- [ ] Kick a rehydrate job for requested window and validate SHA256 manifests.
- [ ] Run redaction script and produce mapping manifest.
- [ ] Upload to auditor share and record artifact metadata with canonical names.

Sampling strategy (recommended):
- Use stratified sampling across: actor_role (admin/devops/user), change type (grant/revoke/role-change), and time buckets (begin/mid/end of quarter).
- Provide at least 30 samples per stratum or 0.5% of total events in the window (whichever is larger).

Fallback evidence when primary logs are partial:
- Provisioning tickets and approval PRs with timestamps.
- CI/CD deploy history showing who merged related PRs.
- Manual access-review exports signed-off by manager.

Acceptance and handoff notes for SOC/ISO evidence pack: 
- Create a top-level index doc that lists artifact id, short description, owner, and direct link.
- Ensure every artifact has a single owner and retention policy note.
- Provide a short walkthrough (10–15 minute) for the auditor on the call using the index doc as the guide.

Pre-rotation snapshot for RBAC v2 cutover (what to capture before major role refactor):
- Full export of current role assignments (CSV).
- Backup of current audit logs (compressed JSONL).
- PRs and design doc for the refactor.
- Post-change verification plan and smoke-test checklist.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting cues for auditors and engineers
- Missing actor_role in sample: provide mapping script output (backfill table) and explain transformation rules.
- SIEM latency: show ingest time vs event timestamp distribution graph and explain retention policy.

Notes and next actions:
- Owner (Priya) to complete G1 tasks and post export sample by 2025-03-12.
- Owner (Ethan) to produce a migration plan to emit normalized fields by next sprint end (2025-03-21).
- Security & Compliance to create the artifact index and follow naming convention by 2025-03-07.

This playbook is intentionally procedural and artifact-first: auditors want a small set of easy-to-reference artifacts plus clear scripts that connect logs->controls->people. Keep one engineer and one compliance owner paired for any on-demand requests during the assessment.
